# v3.00-dev

The version number rolls over from 2.99 to 3.00. Nothing in the application
changes — this release exists because the rollover itself was broken, and the
check that would have blocked it is now fixed.

## Why the number jumped

Versions here move one step per change: the part after the dot counts 00 to 99,
and then the number before the dot goes up by one. So 2.99 is followed by 3.00.
That is the first time this has happened, and it turned out nothing had ever
exercised it.

**This is not a milestone release.** It is the next step after 2.99 and nothing
more. Read it as 2.99 plus one, not as a new generation of the product.

## Fixed

- **The release check no longer blocks the correct version at a rollover.** One
  of the automated checks that runs before a release verifies that the version
  moved by exactly one step. It compared version numbers in a way that worked
  everywhere except at the boundary — where it would have **rejected the correct
  3.00 and accepted a malformed 2.100** instead. It now understands that 99 rolls
  over into the next whole number, and rejects a three-digit value outright with
  an explanation.

  Nothing about how systems find and install updates was affected: that
  comparison only ever asks which version is newer, and it had 3.00 correct all
  along. The fault was in the release check alone, which is why the fix is there
  rather than in the version number.

## Upgrading

No action needed. Systems on the dev channel will offer 3.00 as the next update
in the normal way.
